title: Why Use JSONata from DuckDB?
description: [JSONata](https://jsonata.org/) is an [open query and transformation language for JSON](https://docs.jsonata.org/overview), modelled on XPath. This extension exposes a single scalar function — [`jsonata`](#jsonata) — that evaluates JSONata expressions against DuckDB `JSON` values. Reach for it when DuckDB's native [`json_extract`](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/json_functions.html) chain gets verbose: array predicates, object reshaping, and conditional projections collapse into one expression.

sections.title: What this extension is for
sections.description: DuckDB's built-in [JSON functions](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/json_functions.html) are great for one-field-one-path access. JSONata's strength is everything beyond that — filtering arrays by predicate, building a new object shape, traversing wildcards, and chaining transforms in a single string.

bulletPoints.label: Concise nested paths
bulletPoints.description: Walk dotted [paths](https://docs.jsonata.org/path-operators) like `Account.Order.Product.Price` directly. No quoting per segment, no intermediate `json_extract` calls.

bulletPoints.label: Predicate filters on arrays
bulletPoints.description: `Phone[type="mobile"].number` selects matching elements and projects in one step. See [JSONata predicates](https://docs.jsonata.org/predicate).

bulletPoints.label: Object reshaping
bulletPoints.description: [Object construction](https://docs.jsonata.org/construction) lets you build a fresh JSON object literal — pull only the fields you need, rename them, compute new ones — inside a single [`jsonata`](#jsonata) call.

bulletPoints.label: Higher-order array operations
bulletPoints.description: [`$map`, `$filter`, `$reduce`, `$sort`](https://docs.jsonata.org/higher-order-functions) and friends operate on arrays inside the JSON value. Transformations that would need `unnest` + subquery in plain SQL stay inline.

sections.title: How it works
sections.description: The extension is a pure scalar UDF — no `ATTACH`, no secrets, no network. [`jsonata(expression, json_data)`](#jsonata) parses the expression, evaluates it against the supplied [`JSON`](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/json_functions.html) value, and returns a `JSON` result. A 3-arg form passes a [`bindings`](#jsonata) object so the expression can reference `$variable` names.

bulletPoints.label: One function, two arities
bulletPoints.description: [`jsonata(expr, json)`](#jsonata) for the common case; [`jsonata(expr, json, bindings)`](#jsonata) when the expression needs external `$variables` — typically thresholds, ids, or per-row context lifted from other columns.

bulletPoints.label: Constant-expression optimization
bulletPoints.description: When the `expression` argument is a constant SQL literal — the usual case — the parser runs once and the compiled program is reused for every row. Per-row cost is JSON walk + apply, not parse-and-compile.

bulletPoints.label: JSON in, JSON out
bulletPoints.description: The return type is always [`JSON`](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/json_functions.html). Cast or unnest downstream — `result::VARCHAR`, `result->>'$'`, or `unnest(result::JSON[])` for arrays — exactly like any other DuckDB JSON expression.

bulletPoints.label: Try expressions interactively
bulletPoints.description: The official [JSONata exerciser](https://try.jsonata.org/) is the fastest way to iterate on an expression before pasting it into a SQL string. Same evaluator semantics.

sections.title: Scope and caveats
sections.description: The extension wraps the JSONata language faithfully but lives inside SQL — the surrounding context is DuckDB, not Node.js. A few things are worth knowing up front.

bulletPoints.label: Single function surface
bulletPoints.description: Everything is reached through [`jsonata`](#jsonata). There are no helper UDFs for individual JSONata operators — the expression string carries the whole computation.

bulletPoints.label: Expressions are SQL strings
bulletPoints.description: JSONata expressions live inside a SQL `VARCHAR` literal. Embedded double quotes need SQL escaping; for long expressions, store them in a CTE or a SQL variable and reference by name.

bulletPoints.label: No DuckDB function callbacks
bulletPoints.description: JSONata's JavaScript-binding feature isn't wired up — you can't register a DuckDB UDF as a callable inside the expression. Stick to [JSONata's built-in function library](https://docs.jsonata.org/string-functions).

bulletPoints.label: Performance scales with expression and document size
bulletPoints.description: Deeply-nested documents and complex expressions both cost. For very wide rows, materialize the JSONata projection once into a column instead of re-evaluating it in every downstream query.

useCases.title: Reshape an API payload into table columns
useCases.description: One [`jsonata`](#jsonata) call with an [object-construction](https://docs.jsonata.org/construction) expression replaces a stack of `json_extract_string` projections — and stays readable when nested fields move.

useCases.title: Filter and project nested arrays
useCases.description: `items[status="open" and amount > 100].id` returns only the matching ids. The same logic in DuckDB native JSON functions needs `unnest` plus a subquery.

useCases.title: Aggregate inside a JSON document
useCases.description: [`$sum`, `$count`, `$max`](https://docs.jsonata.org/aggregation-functions) operate on arrays-in-JSON without leaving the expression — useful for per-row roll-ups of an embedded line-item list.

useCases.title: Parameterize an expression at query time
useCases.description: Use the 3-arg [`jsonata(expr, json, bindings)`](#jsonata) form to pass thresholds, user ids, or date cutoffs through `$variables` so a single expression handles many runtime values.
